paths.description: Homepage and primary video-listing template; desktop, narrow viewport, theme/contrast preferences, network, performance, accessibility and crawler states.
Category-index archetype representing browse/navigation into the catalog.
Representative video-detail and paywall surface, selected from the homepage.
Search-results and filtering archetype for the find-content journey.
Membership/pricing surface representing the commercial conversion journey; no purchase or external identity verification was submitted.
Invalid URL used to inspect HTTP/application error messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: The theme does not follow the user color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Dark-emulated and default screenshots are pixel-identical (both 108,316 bytes), computed html color-scheme is normal, and no color-scheme metadata is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light dark support at the root and map surface/text tokens through light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme.

findings.summary: Route and paywall state changes use abrupt swaps
findings.evidence: The CSS/media probe found no view-transition rules; the detail-page screenshot shows the paywall as an abrupt overlay state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for route and paywall state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long-page navigation does not adapt to scroll state
findings.evidence: The homepage is over 21,000 CSS pixels tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or scroll timeline and the mobile header occupies substantial fixed chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Make sticky navigation respond to scroll state, for example by shrinking after scrolling while preserving access.

findings.summary: Stacked on-load overlays obscure primary content and commercial choices
findings.evidence: The join mobile screenshot shows an unsolicited xHamster sign-in panel stacked above a cookie panel that covers most of the viewport; the detail screenshot is dominated by a paywall overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Sequence necessary consent, authentication and paywall UI; show one focused, dismissible layer at a time and do not open sign-in before user intent.

findings.summary: Modal surfaces are built without dialog semantics
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no <dialog> or role=dialog despite the cookie, sign-in and paywall modal surfaces shown in screenshots.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal flows and popover for transient UI, including focus trapping, Escape handling and light-dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: Top chrome crowds the mobile content area
findings.evidence: On 360px captures, age verification, external links, branding and horizontal navigation consume roughly the first 268px before content; controls and labels are visibly clipped at the right edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary navigation and promotions into a compact mobile pattern, keeping the primary content/action in the first viewport.

findings.summary: Narrow layouts overflow and clip content
findings.evidence: At viewport 360x800 the layout primitive reported scrollWidth 769 versus visual viewport 360, 409px of horizontal overflow; search filters, cards and top actions are visibly cut off.
findings.suggestedFix: Use intrinsic grid/flex sizing, min-width:0 and width:100%/max-width constraints; ensure the mobile response is selected without relying on brittle UA behavior.

findings.summary: Reused components do not adapt to available container width
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules, while category cards and search controls are clipped in narrow captures.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/filter/navigation components containment and size-aware container-query layouts, with intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Focus indication and target sizing are inadequate
findings.evidence: The focus probe found key buttons, sign-in/join links and search input with outline:none; Lighthouse also failed target-size, including 16px-high creator links.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear :focus-visible styles and make interactive hit areas at least 24x24 CSS px with adequate spacing (preferably larger for primary touch actions).

findings.summary: The membership journey is obstructed before a user can review and act
findings.evidence: On /join, sign-in and cookie overlays stack over plan choices; the screenshot leaves pricing and the membership CTA partially hidden, adding avoidable detours to the primary flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Wait for explicit sign-in intent, resolve consent in a single layer, then keep plan, renewal terms and CTA together in an unobstructed sequence.

findings.summary: Loading is slow on the measured mobile run
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.2s, Speed Index 7.5s, TBT 350ms and Time to Interactive 25.8s; the CDP trace independently measured FCP/LCP 4.066s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce initial script/style work, and defer below-fold and consent/auth code until needed.

findings.summary: The initial page load is excessively heavy
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 194 requests and 5,404,121 transferred bytes: 3.58MB images and 1.48MB scripts. Forty below-fold images were not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold media, reduce initial result count, right-size assets and gate non-critical scripts behind interaction or idle time.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused JavaScript and CSS ship on first load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 773KiB unused JavaScript and 98KiB unused CSS; individual chunks were 52% to 85% unused and duplicate GTM/gtag payloads total about 304KB transferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by route/feature, load consent/auth/paywall code conditionally, and consolidate analytics initialization.

findings.summary: Multiple controls and links lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name and label: orientation/cart/close controls and many thumbnail/profile links have no accessible text; image inspection also reported 62 images without alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic buttons/anchors and provide concise accessible names; give meaningful images descriptive alt and decorative images empty alt.

findings.summary: Age-verification and badge text fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2.42:1 for white text on the #00bd8f age-verification banner and 4.04:1 for small discount/notification badges, below WCAG minimums.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken or replace the green/red tokens so all text and essential UI meet WCAG AA contrast in every state.

findings.summary: Landmarks, heading order and focus treatment are not robust
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found no main landmark and invalid heading order; the platform probe found zero main/nav/header landmarks and several primary controls with outline:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce semantic header/nav/main/footer landmarks, repair heading hierarchy, and preserve a visible ordered focus path through overlays and content.

findings.summary: Mobile zoom is disabled and content does not reflow cleanly
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found user-scalable=0/maximum-scale=1 in the mobile viewport metadata; narrow evidence also shows clipped content and undersized targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions, then verify 200% zoom/reflow and touch target spacing.

findings.summary: Several images omit intrinsic dimensions
findings.evidence: The image audit found 8 images without width/height, creating avoidable instability risk despite overall CLS remaining in the good range.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio on all imagery and preserve the intended ratio responsively.

findings.summary: The page is not eligible for the back/forward cache
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports Cache-Control: no-store plus cookie modification as an actionable BFCache blocker.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid no-store on public catalog pages where possible and update session state in a BFCache-compatible way.

findings.summary: Some interactive links are not crawlable
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found href="javascript:void(0)" controls and unnamed links; mobile viewport metadata also prevents scaling.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <button> for actions and real href URLs for navigation, with descriptive accessible link text.

findings.summary: No sitemap is exposed at the conventional URL
findings.evidence: Browser navigation to /sitemap.xml returned a plain 404 while robots.txt contains no visible Sitemap directive; canonical and hreflang signals are otherwise present.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap index and reference it from robots.txt, ensuring mirror-domain canonicals and hreflang URLs stay consistent.

findings.summary: Rich listing and video pages lack structured entity metadata
findings.evidence: Probes found zero JSON-LD blocks on the homepage/category and representative video detail; the captured metadata also contains no Open Graph/Twitter preview tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject/ItemList JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata that matches visible titles, thumbnails and canonical URLs.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP protections are weaker than expected
findings.evidence: Eight of 12 cookies lacked Secure, several use SameSite=None, and analytics cookies last 400 days. CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; nosniff and Referrer-Policy are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, use the strictest workable SameSite/HttpOnly settings, remove unsafe CSP allowances via nonces/hashes, and add nosniff and a restrictive Referrer-Policy.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party delivery begin on the initial load
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 14 third-party origins and Google Tag Manager; HAR attributes 191/194 requests and 5.30MB to third-party origins, including two analytics scripts before consent is resolved.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics until consent, reduce vendors/origins, batch necessary events, and document retention/purpose for every identifier.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are overly permissive
findings.evidence: Permissions-Policy grants camera and multiple sensors to all origins; CSP is broad with wildcard/http sources and unsafe script execution, while Referrer-Policy and nosniff are missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Restrict Permissions-Policy to required self/origins, tighten default/script/connect/frame directives, and deploy CSP nonces/hashes plus Trusted Types where applicable.

findings.summary: Overlapping top-layer UI creates a fragile runtime state
findings.evidence: The join capture simultaneously shows sign-in and cookie surfaces, each competing for focus and viewport space rather than one coordinated top-layer state.
findings.suggestedFix: Coordinate modal state in one controller and use native dialog/popover semantics so focus, stacking and dismissal remain predictable.

findings.summary: Renewal and cancellation commitments are not visible beside the trial choice
findings.evidence: The join text exposes a “2-day trial” and price, but the terms probe found no user-visible renewal/cancellation copy or cancellation/terms link, only Privacy Policy, before the CTA area.
findings.suggestedFix: Place recurring price, billing cadence, renewal date and cancellation route directly beside each trial CTA before sign-up.

findings.summary: Media delivery is disproportionate and poorly deferred
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 100 images, 40 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 32 oversized assets and 71 legacy-format URL classifications; images transferred 3.58MB on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP at display-appropriate sizes, lazy-load below-fold media, and avoid fetching duplicate hidden desktop/mobile assets.

findings.summary: The initial page performs substantial work that does not serve the first viewport
findings.evidence: The page loads 159 image requests and 20 scripts, while Lighthouse estimates 773KiB unused JS and 98KiB unused CSS; 191 requests are third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Fetch only first-viewport results initially, virtualize/defer the long feed, conditionally import feature code and postpone background/analytics work.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost dominates the page budget
findings.evidence: HAR reports 5.30MB of 5.40MB transferred from third-party origins; media/CDN images dominate bytes and analytics contributes roughly 304KB of script.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-level media and third-party budgets, enforce lazy loading/caching, and remove or defer integrations that do not support the immediate task.

taskList.title: Repair mobile reflow, zoom, focus and touch targets
Sequence consent, sign-in and paywall into one accessible flow
Cut initial media/script payload and improve LCP
Add accessible names, landmarks, headings and contrast
Tighten CSP, cookies, permissions and pre-consent tracking
Show renewal/cancellation terms beside trial CTAs
Use crawlable links, sitemap and rich metadata
